name: gamescom 2026

days.label: Wednesday
days.hours: Business 09:00–19:00, Entertainment 09:00–19:00 on a trade badge (public Wildcard entry 13:00)
days.note: The only public entry was the €65.50 Wildcard ticket (from 13:00), and it sold out on Aug 5 — so unless you already hold one, Wednesday is trade and media only. Trade badge caveat: some big booths reserve Wednesday (or its morning) for invited press — Xbox's booth doesn't open to visitors until Thursday, and in 2025 Capcom admitted only press until about 11:00.

days.label: Thursday
days.note: Best full public day for hands-on demos — noticeably calmer than Fri–Sat. A trade badge opens the entertainment halls at 09:00, a full hour before the public — the most valuable hour of the week for hands-on demos.

days.label: Friday
days.note: Fills up over the day; mornings still workable for big booths. Trade badges again get in at 09:00, and it is the last day of the business area. gamescom GDQ speedrun showcase starts (Congress Center North).

days.label: Saturday
days.note: Busiest and most expensive day, usually sells out — avoid for hands-on play if you can. City Festival in the evening.

days.label: Sunday
days.note: Most relaxed public day; booths start winding down late afternoon. Free entry possible via completed gamescom epix quests.

onl.note: Hosted by Geoff Keighley, ~2 h show. Free stream on YouTube, Twitch and Steam. In-person tickets (€34.50) sold out.

tickets: Online-only via the official gamescom shop — no on-site box office. Day tickets: Thu/Fri/Sun €31.50 (discounted €22.50), Saturday €41.00; evening tickets from 16:00 €10.50–13.00; family ticket €69.50–86.00; Wednesday Wildcard €65.50 (sold out Aug 5, 2026). Opening Night Live tickets are sold out; Saturday historically sells out before the show. Day tickets include free VRS public transport in the Cologne region.

areas.name: Entertainment area
areas.description: The consumer show: big publisher booths, playable demos, stages, giveaways.

areas.name: Business area
areas.description: Trade visitors, press and accredited creators only (Wed–Fri, 09:00–19:00 Wed / 09:00–20:00 Thu–Fri); closed Sat/Sun. The halls sit at the South entrance, but West is the quieter way in — see Entrances.

areas.name: Event Arena
areas.description: Big stage shows, concerts and esports (incl. Prime League offline finals).

areas.name: Cosplay Village
areas.description: Cosplay contest, photo booths, workshops and the Artist Area.

areas.name: Merchandise Area
areas.description: The only area where exhibitors may sell goods — main merch shopping halls.

areas.name: Cards & Boards Area
areas.description: Card and board game communities and vendors.

areas.name: Indie Area / Indie Arena Booth
areas.description: ~200 indie games from 182 developers — see the Indie Arena Booth exhibitor entry.

areas.name: Retro & Family Area
areas.description: 50 years of gaming history plus family-friendly games — RC drifting, Headis and 8BitDo's retro controllers sit in this half of the hall.

areas.name: Campus Area
areas.description: Universities, education and industry recruiting — roughly half of Hall 10.1, plus a community and youth-work block at D020/E021. Not a demo floor.

areas.name: Hardware & peripherals row
areas.description: Not an officially named zone, but the A–D rows of Hall 10.1 are effectively the hardware hall: MOZA's sim rigs and PXN wheels, Logitech G, Corsair, PNY, Thermaltake, ASRock, a wall of keyboard and gaming-chair brands, a hi-fi corner at A070 — and the retro cluster of Commodore, Atari and MicroProse.

areas.name: Signing Area
areas.description: Content creator autograph and meet-and-greet sessions.

areas.name: gamescom epix
areas.description: Free digital quest program (7 story chapters, started Aug 3) — on-site booth quests, collector cards, and free Sunday tickets for completing all chapters.

areas.name: gamescom GDQ
areas.description: A first-time Games Done Quick speedrunning charity showcase, Aug 28–30, Konrad-Adenauer-Halle (Congress Center North).

areas.name: City Festival
areas.description: Free open-air concerts and gaming zones in Cologne's city center (Ringe), Aug 29–30 evenings.

entrances.lede: Four gates — South, West, East and North — all feed the central Boulevard that runs the length of the grounds from north to south. Which one you pick decides your first half hour. Koelnmesse also steers arriving crowds between gates when a queue backs up, so signs and stewards on the day overrule any plan made in advance.
entrances.trade: The standard advice is "West is best", and it holds — but mainly for the public days. On Wednesday, the trade and media day, the crowds are not there yet and you can take whichever gate suits your route. Thursday and Friday are when West earns it: South and East are carrying the public by then, and West skips both queues without making you fight through the consumer halls. Ask a taxi for West. Whichever gate you use, the badge itself is worth more than the entrance: trade access to the entertainment halls starts at 09:00 every day, a full hour before the public on Thursday and Friday.

list.name: West
list.description: The quiet one, and the trade pick on public days: a few minutes from halls 2–4 and the Confex without crossing a consumer hall, and the best odds of finding a taxi. No station of its own — walk from Köln Messe/Deutz, or ask the driver for West.

list.name: South
list.description: The main entrance and where nearly everyone arriving by rail lands: Köln Messe/Deutz station is right outside, and the business halls 2–4 plus the Confex sit directly behind it. That is also why it is the worst queue on the grounds — it was over capacity by the trade day in 2025. Allow 20–30 minutes on foot from here to Hall 8 at the far end.

list.name: East
list.description: Has its own tram stop (lines 3 and 4, "Koelnmesse"), opens straight into Hall 10 and is a short walk across the plaza to the business area. No longer a secret, and it absorbs South's overflow: in 2025 it was shut at one point and arrivals were routed under the grounds to West instead.

list.name: North
list.description: The shortest walk to the blockbuster halls 6, 7, 8 and 9. The square in front starts filling two hours before doors. Reachable on foot from the tram or by car, not by a station of its own — and from here the business area is the whole length of the Boulevard away.

crowdTips: Saturday is the busiest, priciest day and usually sells out — do hands-on play Thursday or Sunday instead.
Wednesday's Wildcard ticket (entry from 13:00) is the quietest way into the hottest demos, but it sold out on Aug 5 — without one, Thursday morning is the next-best low-crowd window.

On trade Wednesday, a trade badge doesn't open every door: several AAA booths run invited-press-only previews in the morning or skip the day entirely (Xbox 2026: booth opens Thursday; Capcom 2025: press-only until ~11:00). Check a booth's own channels before planning your Wednesday around it.

Arrive well before doors open and pick the entrance nearest your first must-play booth — big booths build 2–4 h queues within the first hour. North is shortest for halls 6–9, East for Hall 10, South for the business halls; see Entrances on the Info tab.

On a trade badge the entertainment halls open at 09:00 every day — an hour before the public on Thursday and Friday. Spend that hour on the one demo you most want to play; it is the closest thing to an empty show floor you will get.
Pick 5–10 must-play booths in advance (official gamescom app + hall plan) and hit your single most-wanted booth right at opening.
Some large booths hand out time slots or fast-lane wristbands in the morning via their own apps — check exhibitors' socials the week before.

A few booths take free bookings online before the show: MOZA Racing's six sim rigs in Hall 10.1 are the clearest example. Booking costs nothing and is the difference between sitting down and watching, so check the websites of any hands-on booth you care about.
Take the train/tram to Koeln Messe/Deutz — day tickets include free VRS public transport; don't drive.
Evening tickets (from 16:00, €10.50–13.00) are a cheap second visit; queues shrink in the last 2–3 hours.
Do gamescom epix quests — completing all chapters can earn a free Sunday ticket.
